correctness.rationale: In coordinates x=r+ps both operations preserve r and add ±(r−c) to s; all translations of each individual fiber occur. An equivalence invariant under these translations is the coset relation of the zero class, an additive subgroup, hence equality or collapse. Any cross-fiber pair with residues r≠c, substituted into the operand slot against an arbitrary element of any fiber, forces identification under the nonzero step r−c; iterating it collapses every fiber, including for p=2. Conversely independent selections of collapsed fibers below the kernel are compatible, and every partition above it is a pullback from the projection quandle. Inclusion gives exactly the glued lattice; the shared relation is counted once. The three additive subgroups give precisely equality, fiber collapse and universality. The numerical counts agree with the corresponding Bell numbers.
residual_risks: The replay exhausts only the two small primes; the translation proof supplies generality. No formal verification is claimed.

value.rationale: The cyclic prime-square shear is a minimal and natural nonconnected test of the module description of Alexander congruences. A complete classification, including exactly when the orbit kernel is forced, describes all permissible quotient kernels; the Bell count quantifies the failure of subgroup-only intuition. This is more useful than a list of small-order examples or re-enumeration of the known lower interval.
